notes: The mission the SPEC demo is about. One document, read by two callers that cannot import
each other: prisma/seed.ts (compiled into the gateway image) and scripts/demo-orchestrator.mjs
(host-side, issues a fresh mission per run). Anything written twice drifts, so this is written
once. `notes` is ignored by both readers — the management API refuses unknown fields.
network.allow is deliberately coarser than permissions.resources. GET reaches the whole acme
org so that a read of acme/secret-project is carried as far as the policy engine and refused
there by the resource scope (demo case 3: the credential could access it, policy blocks it).
DELETE on the repository root is routed for the same reason: case 5 is about deniedActions
refusing a deletion, not about the network never carrying one. A rule narrowed to payments
would refuse both requests one stage earlier and demonstrate the opposite.
pull_request.merge is defence in depth: nothing routes a PUT, so no request reaches the engine
to be judged against it today. It is listed so the action is already refused the day a rule does.
